causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) record register values in '0.1 m3' units, differing 10x from legacy firmware's 'm3' units (E-13).
On 2026-08-01 billing deployed rule BV-17, comparing raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none' (E-12).
For v4.2-metered accounts this unscaled comparison makes a valid reading appear ~10x the historical consumption, misflagging it as anomalous high consumption.
Billing import rejects these flagged, successfully-exported AMI reads with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, 95.5%, E-11).
Rejected reads trigger estimate substitution, producing ESTIMATED-read bills for accounts that actually had a valid high-consumption AMI read.
Customers dispute these ESTIMATED bills, contributing to the Aug-Sep ticket surge (E-07); the mechanism for the remaining ACTUAL-read disputes (59% of disputed bills, E-02) is not yet established.

proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CS) framed the dispute-ticket doubling since August as a slow-response problem, but that framing and a tariff-change explanation were ruled out (E-04; E-01/E-05). The release decision is HOLD: automated Layer-1 verification failed because disputed-bills triage data is reported 1190 records missing while the plan marks the corresponding triage work item DONE — an unresolved contradiction — and no safety predicate/verification could be established, so no part of the intended release scope (ticket triage, dispute-volume monitoring, or the BV-17 correction recommendation to SH-BILL) is being shipped at this time.
